sampling_model.design: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the fully specified finite paired-cell law \(P_{m,h}\), and the label \(m\) is observed.
sampling_model.units: Each normalized unit has \(X=(m,V,J,Z)\), source \(S\), treatment \(T\), observed outcome \(Y=1/2+B\in\{1/2,3/2\}\), and potential outcomes supported on \([0,2]\).
sampling_model.treatment: Conditionally on \(X\), \(S\) and \(T\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\); in the experimental source, treatment is randomized.
sampling_model.overlap: Every design, source, and treatment probability equals \(1/2\), and all Bernoulli outcome probabilities are uniformly inside \((0,1)\) for \(h\in H_m\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the \(2m\) informative gaps are unknown. They are learned globally from capped cell means with an explicit empty-cell rule. On fixed-dimensional separated profiles, the named regular benchmark uses uncapped cell means, estimated signs, empirical influence-score variances, and the joint critical value \(\kappa_{\delta_0}\). Any smooth or polynomial adaptive candidate must charge its own remainder and selection uncertainty.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 derive sharp max/min sensitivity endpoints, while Section 5 replaces them by fixed-temperature Boltzmann approximations for influence-function inference.
The paper defines minimum expected length at a fixed function among globally honest intervals and attains its local-modulus benchmark for monotone and convex regression.
The paper proves the sharp minimax mean-squared-error frontier for an average absolute Gaussian mean by composite priors and Hermite-polynomial estimators.
The paper characterizes adaptive honest confidence intervals for linear functionals through between-class and ordered moduli.
The paper establishes lower bounds on pointwise expected interval length under uniform coverage and shows that honest adaptation can fail.
Section 5.4 gives a fixed-smoothing Wald interval and leaves data-driven tuning for the shortest confidence interval open.
Theorem 2 and Corollary D.1 establish asymptotic inference for deterministic entropic regularization under margin and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper proves minimax point-estimation rates for nonsmooth discrete-distribution functionals using best-polynomial approximation and unbiased discrete moments.
The paper constructs one-at-a-time functional intervals by constrained likelihood-ratio inversion in linear Gaussian inverse problems.

body.tldr: Sharp data-fusion sensitivity endpoints are averages of absolute paired-cell gaps, so exact and near ties create a confidence problem that fixed smoothing does not resolve. The project computes the local minimum expected summed length of jointly honest endpoint intervals throughout the full heterogeneous gap cube, determines the least multiplicative price paid by one profile-independent procedure, and constructs a finite-sample honest family attaining that price. Exact-tie and low-information results provide the tractable reductions; a mixed tie--boundary slice and a Bernstein-certified likelihood program make the open higher-information full-profile frontier explicitly falsifiable, including every logarithmic factor.

project_justification.gap: Published data-fusion work identifies the max/min endpoints and uses fixed smoothing, while confidence adaptation theory concerns linear or ordered functionals and absolute-functional theory concerns point risk. None evaluates the connected-interval local oracle and simultaneous adaptation cost for the paired binomial endpoint experiment.
project_justification.niche: The fixed learnable subclass isolates the statistical cost of ties without nuisance ambiguity, retains both causal endpoints and joint coverage, and exposes heterogeneous profiles that a scalar margin condition removes.
project_justification.fill: The project combines exact paired-binomial composite tests, moment-matched alternatives, a finite Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy with an explicit size bound, and nested inversion to give an explicit oracle profile, a sharp oracle ratio, and one implementable honest endpoint family.

body.related_work: ColnetMayerEtAl2024 surveys the broader trial--observational fusion literature without a tie-adaptive endpoint-confidence result. LannersRudinVolfovskyParikh2025 supplies the causal sensitivity endpoints and the applied Project STAR motivation; its fixed-temperature inference is an input, not a theorem-level target. CaiLowXia2013 supplies the closest local expected-length criterion, but its ordered shape-constrained Gaussian geometry does not cover a nonlinear absolute average. CaiLow2011 supplies the composite-prior and polynomial tools for the absolute-value cusp, but only for minimax point estimation. CaiLow2004 and Low1997 organize honest adaptation for linear functionals and furnish coverage-to-testing logic. LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025 explicitly leaves shortest-interval smoothing selection open, while BenMichael2025 handles deterministic growing regularization under margin conditions. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 motivates factorial moments for sparse cells, and BatllePatilStanleyOwhadiKuusela2024 motivates finite-sample test inversion but is confined to constrained linear Gaussian inverse problems.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact-tie statement covers every \(n,m\), whereas the displayed full-profile formula is asserted only when \(n\le\sqrt m/(20a_m^2)\). Beyond this regime, the corner mixture is statistically distinguishable and the deficit formula cannot be extrapolated. The Bernstein-certified likelihood hierarchy supplies explicit variables, constraints, and a per-slice size bound, but it is not itself a frontier: the solver must establish a sufficient certificate degree, evaluate the mixed tie--boundary slice, control connected-hull length, and prove an implementable uniform upper bound.
body.honest_scope: All endpoint, compatibility, oracle, and adaptation claims are stated for the normalized experiment with observed outcomes in \(\{1/2,3/2\}\) and potential outcomes in \([0,2]\). Arbitrary outcome units and the conventional outer ATE interval appear only as implementation-level definitional consequences and receive no theorem-level credit; the pushforward does not alter \(h\), \(H_m\), \(a_m\), \(b\), or \(k\). The mathematical kernel concerns the displayed fixed union of paired-cell Bernoulli experiments and joint confidence intervals for its two sharp endpoints; it does not claim unrestricted nonparametric data-fusion inference. The exact-tie, low-information, causal-completion, positivity, and nuisance-learning statements are traction that must be independently proved. The higher-information profile \(\Phi_{n,m}(h)\), the sharp factor \(q_{n,m}\), the mixed tie--boundary slice, and the attaining interval family remain open. For fixed \(m\) and \(\xi\), the separated-profile check uses the explicitly centered and jointly calibrated procedure \(C^{\mathrm{sign}}_{n,m}\), requires an \(n^{-1/2}\) oracle and a bounded oracle ratio, and asserts endpoint-center equivalence only. At \(h=0\), the profile must collapse to \(k\min\{a_m,m^{1/4}/\sqrt n\}\).
